sources.name: Michigan DHHS county death tables (no small-number hiding)
sources.notes: pipeline/statefill.py. Fills ONLY cells CDC hid (1-9), and only for causes where Michigan agrees with CDC (within 10% or 2 deaths) in 90%+ of county-years CDC publishes. Drug-induced and diabetes-related tables are not used (wider definitions than CDC's).

sources.name: WONDER UCD 1999-2018, county x 5-year totals
sources.notes: Spans 1999-2003, 2004-08, 2009-13, 2014-18, one request per cause and span. Shown by the "5-year totals" switch. Big drops in hidden counties for suicide, firearm and the diseases; little change for rare causes (homicide, falls, early overdose), where zero-death counties move into the hidden 1-9 band.

sources.name: WONDER Provisional, county x 5-year totals (2019-2023, 2021-2025)
sources.notes: Pulled 2026-10-07 - residence and occurrence, spans 2019-2023 and 2021-2025, 16 causes (all but all-cause), one request per cause x span, ~1 a minute (WONDER returns HTTP 429 when rushed). 2025 is provisional; re-pull 2021-2025 once 2025 is final.

sources.name: New York State vital statistics Table 38 (county deaths by selected cause, no small-number hiding)
sources.notes: pipeline/statefill.py, same fill-and-check rules as mi_mdhhs plus a per-year check (years where under 80% of county-years agree are skipped - e.g. a changed table layout). Columns are matched by name and aligned from the right (2008-2021 tables have an unlabeled Total column). Not used - Alcohol Poisoning (narrower than alcohol-induced), Pneumonia (no flu). Homicide includes legal intervention; agreement 92%.

sources.name: Ohio Public Health Data Warehouse, mortality
sources.gap: Ohio's disclosure rule doesn't hide small death counts, so all 88 counties x every cause could be filled, 2007 on.
sources.notes: Blocked 2026-10-07: the Claude in Chrome extension has no permission for publicapps.odh.ohio.gov, and the network allowlist blocks it from the cloud and the desktop shell. Needs the site allowed in the extension, then a Chrome pull like NM/PA.

sources.name: New Mexico IBIS death queries (county x year, 15 leading causes + overdose)
sources.notes: Pulled 2026-10-07 with the Chrome script (one query per cause; the builder's hidden CauseDrug2/CauseDespair fields must be disabled or they filter the result). Overdose uses CDC's exact codes (X40-X44, X60-X64, X85, Y10-Y14). Agreement with CDC 87-98%; stroke (77%) and flu, kidney, COVID (<90%) are skipped automatically.

sources.name: Pennsylvania EDDIE death statistics (county x year)
sources.notes: Pulled 2026-10-07: one table with 15 causes x 67 counties x 1990-2024 (takes ~60 s to render). Chrome blocks downloads from this site, so the file was carried to GitHub in the tab (window.name) and attached there. Agreement with CDC 98-100% on every cause. Firearm includes legal intervention (CDC's firearm measure does too). No exact overdose match (EDDIE's poisoning/drug-induced are wider).

sources.name: NCHS restricted-use mortality files with full geography
sources.notes: Researchers only, under a data-use agreement; results can't be published at small-count county level. Not usable for a public map.

sources.name: National Violent Death Reporting System
sources.notes: Public WISQARS views are state-level; case-level data is restricted.

sources.name: IHME US county cause-specific mortality estimates
sources.notes: Releases: 1980-2014 (21 causes, 5-yearly), 2000-2019 by race/ethnicity (19 causes, annual), single-cause follow-ups. License is non-commercial and forbids redistributing the data or derivative works (user agreement section 6); MortalGIS republishes per-county values in its JSON files, so it can't use them. Revisit only with written permission from IHME.

sources.name: Gun Violence Archive
sources.notes: Copyrighted, proprietary aggregation; use limited to the query tool or a licensing agreement. Scraped copies on GitHub/Kaggle are unlicensed. The Trace's data hub forbids redistribution too. No openly licensed nationwide located gun-death dataset exists; for gun suicides and totals use state sources.

sources.name: State vital statistics portals with lower small-number thresholds
